note: The Variations menu. Each variation has its rules in the engine (packages/chess-core/src/engine.js, chosen by the FEN prefix in `start`), a one-page rule sheet, a short lesson with Rooky and the animal friends as bots. `differs` marks a rule that is not like chess, in the sheet and in the lesson. Lesson and exercise lines are spoken from guide.json (`line`), recorded by tools/voice/record-guide.py. Variations with status `soon` are shown but cannot be played yet.

variants.name: Chaturanga
variants.tagline: The very first chess, from India
variants.blurb: The ancient Indian game that every kind of chess grew from. Its name means the four parts of an army: foot soldiers, horses, elephants and chariots. The pieces start where you know them, but the counsellor and the elephant move in the old, short way.

pieces.name: Raja
pieces.moves: One square in any direction, like the king today.

pieces.name: Mantri
pieces.moves: One square on a slant, and no further. He stands where the queen stands and grew into her.

pieces.name: Gaja
pieces.moves: Jumps exactly two squares on a slant, over anything in between. It stands where the bishop stands and grew into it.

pieces.name: Ashva
pieces.moves: Jumps in an L, just like the knight.

pieces.name: Ratha
pieces.moves: Slides along rows and columns, just like the rook.

pieces.name: Padati
pieces.moves: One square forward, even on the first move, and captures one square forward on a slant. On the far side he becomes a Mantri.

rules.title: The same start
rules.text: Every piece starts on the square of the piece it grew into: the Mantri on the queen's square, the Gaja on the bishops' squares.

rules.title: No castling
rules.text: The king walks to safety one step at a time.

rules.title: No en passant
rules.text: Soldiers never move two squares, so there is nothing to take in passing.

rules.title: Checkmate wins
rules.text: Trap the enemy king so it cannot escape, just like in chess.

rules.title: A bare king loses
rules.text: Capture every enemy piece except the king and you win. If they can capture your last piece straight back, it is a draw instead.

rules.title: No move at all loses
rules.text: If a player is not in check but has no legal move, the player who trapped them wins. In chess this is stalemate, a draw.

rules.title: Draws
rules.text: Repeating the same position, or fifty moves with no capture and no soldier move, can end the game as a draw, as in chess.

notes: Rules changed from place to place over the centuries. Chackmate plays one common version, close to shatranj, the Persian game that came from it.
Move lists write the Mantri as Q and the Gaja as B, after the pieces they became.

lesson.title: Chaturanga: chess as it began
objectives: Move the Mantri and the Gaja
Win the old ways: bare king and no moves

hints: One small step, on a slant.
Exactly two squares on a slant.
The Gaja jumps over the pawn on c5, and can capture on b6.
Your chariot can reach Black's last piece.

exercises.explain: In chaturanga a soldier always becomes a Mantri, the counsellor.

hints: Black's pawn is stuck. Can the king move anywhere?
Use the chariot to guard the b-file.

variants.name: Chess960
variants.blurb: The pieces on the back row are shuffled before every game, so you have to think from the very first move.

variants.name: Xiangqi
variants.blurb: Chinese chess, played on the lines of the board with a river in the middle, cannons, and generals who never leave their palace.

variants.name: King of the Hill
variants.tagline: Race your king to the middle
variants.blurb: Win by checkmate, or by walking your king safely onto one of the four centre squares.

variants.name: Three-check
variants.blurb: Give check three times and you win, even before checkmate.
